Today’s poem

The Fair Hanger

Little Wonderer made a fine scale out of string,
a hanger, two cups, and a hook for the swing.
In one cup, a washer. In one, feathers piled.
They balanced. They balanced! The little one smiled.

“Hold still,” said the big one. “A balance is shy.
The tiniest puff sends one cup way up high.
Don’t giggle, don’t wiggle, don’t breathe, and don’t—” Oh.
A tickle had started somewhere down below.

“Ah… ah…” went the little one. “AH-CHOO!” And the air
was suddenly full of white feathers up there.
The feather cup flew up. The washer cup fell.
The hanger swung sideways and rang like a bell.

Big Wonderer waited for feathers to land.
The little one sniffed with a cup in each hand.
“My scale has just measured, and scales never lie:
a sneeze is much heavier than feathers. Goodbye!”
